cards.text: Jesus has just bowed His head and yielded up His spirit on the cross. It's the day of Preparation, and the next day is a High Sabbath. The Jews don't want the bodies left on the crosses during the Sabbath, so they go to Pilate, the Roman governor.

cards.question: The Jews ask Pilate to have the ___ broken and the bodies removed.
The soldiers come and break the legs of both men who were crucified with Jesus.

cards.text: The soldiers work their way down the line. Now they come to Jesus.

cards.question: When the soldiers reach Jesus, do they break His legs too?

answers.text: No because He is already dead
Yes just like the other two men

cards.text: Instead, one of the soldiers takes a spear and pierces Jesus' side.

cards.question: When the soldier's spear pierces Jesus' side, ___ and ___ flow out immediately.

cards.text: The writer hits PAUSE on the story right here. “The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true.”

cards.question: The one who saw the blood and water says he knows he's telling the truth. Why is he telling it?

answers.text: So that you also may believe
So that the soldier is judged
So that Pilate hears about it

cards.text: Then the writer says these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled. And he points to two Scriptures, not one.

cards.question: The first Scripture says, “Not one of His bones will be broken.” The soldiers leaving Jesus' legs alone fits that Scripture.
The second Scripture says, “They will look on the One they have pierced.” Which moment at the cross does it point to?

answers.text: The legs of the two men

cards.text: Afterward, a man named Joseph of Arimathea steps forward. He's a disciple of Jesus, but he's been keeping it a secret.

cards.question: Why has Joseph of Arimathea kept it secret that he's a disciple of Jesus?

answers.text: He is afraid of the Jews
He is afraid of the Romans
Jesus asked him to keep quiet

cards.text: Now Secret Joseph walks right up to Pilate and asks to remove the body of Jesus. Friend, I get nervous asking for an extra cookie box. This man is asking the GOVERNOR.

cards.question: Pilate refuses to let Joseph of Arimathea remove the body of Jesus.

cards.text: Joseph isn't alone. Nicodemus comes too, the Pharisee who had come to Jesus at night back in John 3:1-2, and he doesn't come empty-handed.

cards.question: Nicodemus brings a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about ___ pounds.

cards.text: SEVENTY-FIVE POUNDS. I tried to lift a tub of cookie dough half that size once. ONCE. Then the two men take the body of Jesus and wrap it with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.

cards.question: Joseph and Nicodemus wrap the body of Jesus with the spices in ___ cloths.

cards.text: Now, in the place where Jesus was crucified, there's a garden.

cards.question: What is in the garden near where Jesus was crucified?

answers.text: A new tomb where no one had been laid
An old tomb already holding many bodies
A stone room for storing burial spices

cards.question: Joseph and Nicodemus have to carry Jesus far from where He was crucified to find a tomb.

cards.text: With the day of Preparation on them and the tomb close by, they lay Jesus there. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Trust me, this story is not finished.

findings.problem: The opening card says Jesus 'has just bowed His head and yielded up His spirit on the cross.' That fact comes from John 19:30, which is outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only John 19:31.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Several story cards in this stop are bare retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 4 ('The soldiers work their way down the line. Now they come to Jesus.') and card 6 ('Instead, one of the soldiers takes a spear and pierces Jesus' side.') are examples. The fix doesn't need to be a joke, since this is a solemn moment, but it does need some warmth or a storyteller's line.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer 'So that you also may believe' is the exact Bible wording and speaks to the reader as 'you.' The wrong answers ('So that the soldier is judged', 'So that Pilate hears about it') are plain paraphrases about people in the scene. That makes the right answer sound more like the Bible than the others, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Card 10 already says 'these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.' Card 11 then quotes 'Not one of His bones will be broken' and asks whether the unbroken legs fit that Scripture. Card 10 has already given away the answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Now Secret Joseph walks right up to Pilate...', 'Friend, I get nervous asking for an extra cookie box.' and 'This man is asking the GOVERNOR.' Only the opening card can be longer than 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: 'SEVENTY-FIVE POUNDS.', 'I tried to lift a tub of cookie dough half that size once.', 'ONCE.' and 'Then the two men take the body...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'purple' is a color, while 'linen' and 'wool' are materials. The answers aren't all the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The last story card has 3 sentences, which is over the limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over ('And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Trust me, this story is not finished.') almost copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
